query: I'm writing tests for a Python project and keep reinventing how to structure shared setup, handle async code paths, and fake external calls — want the established idioms instead of guessing.
rationale: caller wants a reference of idiomatic test-writing patterns, not generated tests or workflow enforcement

query: There's a website whose look I want to reuse — I need the actual underlying color values, spacing scale, and component styles pulled out, not just eyeballing it in devtools.
rationale: caller wants concrete design tokens lifted from a live site, not a newly proposed design system

query: I want one consistent toolkit that covers everything from the first design doc through cleanup at the end of a feature, not a pile of one-off scripts for each stage.
rationale: caller wants a single coherent command set spanning the whole build lifecycle rather than scattered ad-hoc scripts

query: Make sure new commits stay consistent with how the rest of this codebase is written before they land.
rationale: caller wants conformance to existing conventions enforced, not a security/spec-compliance or PR-automation review

query: This function has grown into something nobody can hold in their head anymore — help me carve it back down to something readable.
rationale: Wants an existing overgrown piece of code reduced, not a new-implementation minimalism check.

query: The site feels sluggish to users but I don't actually know what's causing it — I need to find the real culprit and confirm the fix actually helped before I ship it.
rationale: caller wants a diagnose-fix-verify loop for a slow site, not just a measurement report

query: this feature is way too big to build in one shot — help me carve it into pieces I can actually ship one at a time
rationale: wants a big feature decomposed into shippable increments, without the ticket-tracker publishing (to-tickets) or full document-writing (writing-plans) angle

query: I want to make sure nobody starts writing code on this feature until we've nailed down exactly what it's supposed to do, written down and agreed.
rationale: caller wants a gate enforcing a written specification before implementation begins

query: Make this deck look like it actually came from the company behind Claude — same colors, same type, no guessing at the palette.
rationale: caller wants an artifact styled to match a specific company's established visual identity

query: I've got a recorded walkthrough and need to know exactly what happens on screen, plus what's being said, without watching the whole thing myself.
rationale: Wants a video's visual and spoken content extracted and summarized on the agent's behalf.

query: I need direct low-level control of a real browser process, not a wrapper library, and it should fix its own approach when a selector stops working instead of just failing.
rationale: caller wants direct protocol-level control with self-repairing helpers, not a scraping/automation wrapper

query: I keep reaching for a library or writing custom code for things the language already gives me for free — push back and make me justify that before I add anything.
rationale: Wants a discipline that defaults to native/stdlib solutions and questions unnecessary complexity before code is written.

query: let a couple of different models each take an independent pass at this, then reconcile their answers into something better than either alone, without paying full price for the biggest model on everything
rationale: wants multi-model cross-checked answer synthesis at lower cost, distinct from swarm/hive-mind topology or consensus mechanics

query: I need a tally of who showed up broken down by congregation, with variant spellings of the same place merged instead of double counting.
rationale: Wants a normalized per-organization attendance count that collapses name variants, not a raw attendee total or a distinct-name list.

query: there's a pile of inbound messages about an upcoming event — tie each one to the right attendee record and prep a reply queued to go out
rationale: wants inbound message triage against attendee records with an auto-drafted reply, for an event-registration context distinct from software-issue triage skills

query: Before I can pull a single page, I need the API key and client wired up correctly.
rationale: Wants initial credential/client setup specifically, not the scraping or search usage itself.

query: Our app needs a built-in way to pull clean text and data out of arbitrary web pages as a shipped feature, not just for a one-off research task.
rationale: caller wants page-extraction wired into their own product code, distinct from an ad-hoc scrape action

query: Get my whole web-data toolkit running in one shot — fetching pages, running searches, clicking through sites, and having the credentials already wired in.
rationale: caller wants the full install-everything suite rather than one individual firecrawl capability

query: how much of last sprint's pipeline time went to re-fixing stuff we broke ourselves versus real new work, and could we have caught it before pushing
rationale: wants a cost breakdown of wasted CI cycles from self-inflicted failures vs. genuine feature work

query: the site feels slower since the last release and I want hard numbers proving it, before and after
rationale: wants before/after web perf measurement to confirm a regression, distinct from LLM-model benchmarking or generic system profiling

query: Right after we push a release, I want something continuously watching the pages for anything going wrong — broken visuals, slow loads, new console errors — so we catch it before customers do, without re-running the whole release process.
rationale: caller wants standalone post-release health watching, distinct from the deploy pipeline itself

query: Before you do anything that can't be undone, stop and check with me first, and keep a record of what changed along the way.
rationale: caller wants a conservative mode that pauses on irreversible actions and logs side effects

query: I'm picking this back up after a break and don't want to re-explain everything I already figured out — just get me back to where I left off.
rationale: caller wants a prior saved session state reloaded and resumed without re-briefing

query: We're starting from a blank slate visually — need a documented, defendable set of visual decisions the team can point back to later, based on what similar products do, instead of everyone guessing individually.
rationale: caller wants a from-scratch design system built and recorded, not extracted from an existing site or an audit of one

query: I can't decide what direction this should go in — generate a handful of different looks so I can compare them side by side and pick one.
rationale: Wants multiple generated visual options to compare and iterate on, not an audit of an existing design.

query: I need to lock down merges to this branch until further notice — we just had an incident and nothing should land except the critical fix.
rationale: caller wants a merge/commit freeze put in place to protect a branch, not confirmation prompts on individual actions

query: Before this plan moves forward I want the business case, the interface, the codebase, and how developers will feel using it all checked automatically, with a call made on each, without me sitting in on every single pass.
rationale: caller wants every review lens run end-to-end with automated decisions, not one review type they have to babysit

query: I need one system that can click through my app like a user, probe it for holes an attacker would find, try out a few different visual directions, and steer the whole build-to-ship process without me handing off between separate tools each step.
rationale: Wants one unified workflow spanning browser QA, security probing, design exploration, and end-to-end product orchestration in a single pass.

query: something's broken and I keep patching symptoms without ever figuring out what's actually going wrong — make me pin that down before touching code
rationale: wants enforced root-cause diagnosis before any fix, distinguishing from mattpocock/diagnose's build-a-repro-loop emphasis

query: Someone outside the team is going to ask how this project is doing — I need a quick current snapshot pulled from what's been shipped and what's still outstanding, not a deep-dive.
rationale: caller wants a forward-looking stakeholder status snapshot, not a backward-looking sprint retrospective

query: I have a rough startup idea and want someone to push back hard on it — is there really a market, why hasn't this been done, what's the smallest version I could test.
rationale: caller wants YC-style forcing-question brainstorming to stress-test a startup idea

query: Before we commit to building this, I want someone to push back hard on whether we're taking on too much or too little from a business standpoint.
rationale: caller wants a strategic/business-scope challenge on a plan before implementation, distinct from a technical architecture review

query: Before people start adopting this tool, I want to see the experience through a total newcomer's eyes, compared honestly against what competitors offer, with concrete next steps — not just a number.
rationale: caller wants persona-driven, competitor-benchmarked improvement steps rather than a simple scored audit report

query: The model keeps doing the wrong thing because my instructions to it are apparently open to interpretation — tighten them up before that happens again.
rationale: Wants ambiguous prompt/plan wording rewritten to reduce misinterpretation and downstream errors.

query: Click through the app like a real visitor, find what's actually broken, fix it yourself with real commits, and prove it's better than before.
rationale: Wants exploratory testing that also fixes found bugs and shows before/after proof, not just detection or a scoped test run.

query: before this lands I want two different AI reviewers to argue over it and catch security holes a single pass would miss
rationale: wants adversarial dual-model review targeting security/trust issues pre-merge, not just a style/spec checklist

query: getting this project ready to go live for the first time — want the credentials and config squared away before anything ships
rationale: wants initial infra/credential provisioning done before the very first deploy, not the deploy execution itself

query: I want to take my current branch, make sure it's tested and merges cleanly, bump the version, log what changed, and get it queued for review — all as one step, not a deploy afterward.
rationale: caller wants the merge-test-changelog-PR sequence as a single command, stopping short of deploy

query: Before we start planning this out, let's actually talk through the open questions and lock in the choices we're making so we're not starting from a blank slate.
rationale: caller wants decisions and context captured up front, before any planning artifact is produced

query: I want a single repeatable loop that carries a raw idea from first conversation to live, tested, merged code without me stitching each stage together by hand.
rationale: Wants the whole suite-level delivery pipeline, not any one phase of it.

query: Before we start building, I want someone with no memory of this conversation to look at what we're about to do with fresh eyes and confirm it still makes sense, after digging into whatever we don't fully understand yet.
rationale: caller wants a clean-context sanity check plus research on unknowns before execution starts

query: Before we call this feature finished, go check it actually does what it's supposed to, and patch anything that's still broken.
rationale: Wants an active check-and-repair pass on finished-looking work, not just a verification gate that blocks the claim.

query: Before I download anything, I want to peek inside a dataset — what fields it has, what its parts look like, and whether it contains certain text — without pulling the whole thing.
rationale: caller wants to browse and preview a hosted dataset's structure and content before committing to it

query: we're paying for the same or nearly-the-same LLM calls over and over and I want to avoid re-running a prompt when something close enough was already answered.
rationale: caller wants to cut redundant LLM spend by matching near-identical prior prompts

query: Help me design how a change moves from a build through staging into production, including how we'd back out if a release goes bad.
rationale: caller wants pipeline/promotion/rollback design, not a single one-shot deploy execution or post-deploy monitoring

query: I want to simulate someone actually clicking through the whole signup-to-checkout flow across different browsers and catch anything that visually looks off compared to before, without me manually clicking through it every release.
rationale: caller wants full end-to-end user-journey simulation with visual regression detection across browsers, not generic scraping/automation or unit tests

query: need to screen a batch of candidate compounds computationally before anything touches a lab bench
rationale: in-silico molecular property screening before physical experiments

query: want to try out a quantum algorithm idea without needing access to real quantum hardware
rationale: wants to simulate/test quantum circuit logic without physical hardware

query: I've got a big batch of individual-cell gene expression readouts, full of noise and dropouts, and I need to sort them into biologically meaningful groups and see what's driving the differences between those groups.
rationale: caller needs a single-cell RNA-seq QC/clustering/DE workflow without naming the tool

query: I have relational data — things connected to other things — and want to train a model that predicts new connections or classifies the whole structure, not just tabular rows.
rationale: caller needs a graph-structured ML workflow (node/link/graph prediction) without naming the library

query: I want to load a pretrained language model, run inference on it, and fine-tune it on my own data, all in Python.
rationale: caller wants the core HF Transformers workflow (load/infer/fine-tune), distinct from the JS runtime or the training-orchestration-only sibling

query: I need to move this PHP app from the previous major framework release to the newest one without breaking anything already running in production.
rationale: caller wants a guided major-version framework upgrade, not a generic dependency bump

query: This bug is slippery and I keep patching symptoms — I won't touch the code again until I have a reliable, repeatable way to tell whether a change actually worked.
rationale: caller wants a disciplined loop that blocks further edits until a trustworthy pass/fail signal exists, fix included

query: Our team keeps using different words for the same concept across the codebase and conversations, and it drifts over time — I want that kept aligned as the project evolves, not just a one-time cleanup.
rationale: caller wants ongoing terminology alignment maintained over time, not a one-shot glossary extraction

query: We've been going back and forth on this feature for an hour — turn everything we've settled on into one proper requirements doc and post it to the tracker.
rationale: Wants conversational context turned into a formal published requirements document, not a plan broken into individual issues.

query: split this plan into independent chunks people can grab off the backlog, and flag which ones need a human to weigh in versus which the agent can just run with
rationale: wants a plan decomposed into independently pickable work items with human-in-loop flags, distinct from the generic breakdown that doesn't publish or classify

query: Different people on the team keep calling the same concept by different names in code and in conversation, and I want that pinned down into one agreed vocabulary everyone has to use.
rationale: caller wants a shared glossary extracted and enforced across the codebase
note: collides with mattpocock/domain-modeling ('build and sharpen a project domain model with ubiquitous language and CONTEXT.md maintenance') — both center on the same shared-terminology artifact with no clean honest split.

query: I just said something and I can tell it didn't land the way I meant — I want to try explaining it again, differently.
rationale: caller wants to re-pitch a message that missed its mark

query: One entry in the catalog points to a dead link and its rating doesn't actually match what's backing it up — I want that single item fixed with citations, not a whole sweep.
rationale: caller wants a targeted single-entry correction with sourced justification, not a bulk triage pass or new-entry discovery

query: I found a bunch of candidate skills but haven't verified anything about them yet — park them somewhere flagged as unverified so a human can check before any of them go live.
rationale: Wants unverified discoveries staged with flags for human validation, not a full research-and-publish pass or an automated batch run.

query: Some entries in the registry seem to require steps that don't actually exist, and others aren't connected to anything at all — I need to know exactly where the structure breaks down and what order to fix it in.
rationale: caller wants the specific structural breakage in the skill dependency graph found and prioritized, not schema validation or generic knowledge-graph mapping

query: What's the current buzz around this topic across forums, video, and prediction markets over the past month — I don't want to check five different sites myself.
rationale: caller wants a time-boxed multi-source sweep synthesized for them instead of manual cross-platform checking

query: Before we ship, run a full sweep on this screen — contrast, spacing, animation timing, whether a screen reader could even use it — not just my gut feeling.
rationale: Wants a broad, multi-dimension interface quality audit covering accessibility, visuals, and interaction, not a single heuristic checklist.

query: These three code changes don't depend on each other — I want them worked on at the same time instead of one after the other to save wall-clock time.
rationale: caller wants independent subtasks fanned out concurrently to cut total time, not a topology-managed swarm or a review-gated execution pipeline

query: Before I show this diff to anyone else, get a fresh set of eyes on it now so problems surface before they spread.
rationale: Wants a proactive isolated-context review pass before sharing work, catching issues early rather than processing feedback already received.

query: I want one consistent way to work a coding task end to end—figuring out what to build, breaking it into steps, running things in parallel where I can, and working through failures methodically instead of guessing—all under one discipline.
rationale: caller wants a single unified process covering the whole agentic dev lifecycle, not a point tool

query: Before I write any fix, I want solid proof of what's actually broken and why, stripped down to the smallest case that shows it, not just a hunch.
rationale: caller wants root-cause confirmation via a minimal reproduction before any corrective code is written

query: don't want my in-progress changes clobbering the checkout I already have open for something else
rationale: wants concurrent isolated working copies instead of one shared checkout

query: Stop telling me 'this should work now' — actually run it and show me real output before you say it's fixed.
rationale: Wants a hard gate requiring executed evidence before any completion claim, distinct from active diagnose-and-repair skills.

query: Before I write any code on this multi-step feature I want it broken into small pieces someone else could pick up independently, spelled out clearly first.
rationale: caller wants an upfront implementation plan decomposed into independent sub-tasks
note: collides with addy-osmani/planning-and-task-breakdown ('decomposing features into manageable vertical slices') — both are pre-coding decomposition-into-independent-units skills with no honest distinguishing angle available.

query: I want the model to pick up the pattern from a handful of examples I paste into the prompt, no retraining involved.
rationale: caller wants in-context adaptation via example conditioning rather than fine-tuning or optimization frameworks

query: want the page to feel like the visitor is piloting through space as they move down it, no jump cuts between sections
rationale: wants an immersive continuous-motion landing page experience

query: My UI works fine but it screams 'built by an AI' — generic spacing, default everything — I need it to look like a real designer touched it.
rationale: caller wants the generic AI-generated look polished away, distinct from a usability or accessibility scoring pass

query: not sure how a prop works in this programmatic video library and need to check the official reference instead of guessing
rationale: wants to consult reference/API documentation while implementing, as opposed to scaffolding a new project or rendering output

query: I've built out my video composition and now need to actually export the finished file — encoding, output format, and how long that final pass takes.
rationale: caller needs to produce the final rendered video output, not build or preview the composition

query: I need my vector store kept in sync across multiple machines in real time, with search results that don't all cluster around the same few answers.
rationale: caller wants low-latency distributed sync plus diversity-aware retrieval, not the basic single-node similarity search or the whole fused memory platform

query: need to point an automated browser at a page, click through a flow, and grab a screenshot as proof it worked
rationale: generic browser-automation need
note: collides with garrytan/browse (directed navigation + screenshots) and intelligentcode-ai/user-tester (Playwright/Puppeteer E2E, cross-browser) — description offers no feature not already covered by one of those siblings

query: A bunch of background jobs finished running in parallel and I need their outputs pulled together in one place, with a clear read on which ones actually succeeded versus failed.
rationale: caller wants post-run output aggregation and success/failure status, not spawning, routing, or latency benchmarking of the workers

query: I want to keep the interactive reasoning conversation going in one place while shipping background jobs off to run elsewhere, and have the results flow back automatically without me babysitting each one.
rationale: Wants a fused hybrid pattern that spawns background workers, collects their output, and coordinates it with the interactive session — the full loop, not just one piece.

query: I need to spin up a whole cloud-hosted swarm of agents, manage the platform and billing side, and also train distributed neural nets across it — as one connected system, not separately.
rationale: caller wants the combined swarm+cloud-platform+neural-training package, not any single piece alone

query: I need people to log in, get their own isolated environment spun up on demand, get billed for usage, and see it all listed for others to browse and pick from.
rationale: Wants the full platform lifecycle — auth, provisioning, billing, and a public listing — not the neural training or swarm topology pieces of the broader suite.

query: I want several agents to independently weigh in on a decision and have their votes combined into one answer that sticks around across sessions.
rationale: caller wants voting-based agreement among specialized workers plus persistent shared memory, not load-balanced topology or the whole platform bundle

query: I want certain checks to run automatically at specific points in the agent's workflow — and some things to happen on a schedule when I'm not watching — without me manually triggering them each time.
rationale: caller wants lifecycle hooks and scheduled background tasks designed for automated quality gates

query: want the agent to actually get better at this kind of task over many separate sessions, not just start fresh every time
rationale: wants general adaptive cross-session knowledge-building, as opposed to a specific storage backend (reasoningbank-agentdb) or pure decision-strategy tuning (reasoningbank-intelligence)

query: My agent setup is a patchwork of separate tools for remembering things, talking to my repo host, and getting multiple agents to agree with each other — I want it all consolidated under one roof, fully caught up to the latest version.
rationale: caller wants the unified apex platform instead of juggling the individual subsystems separately

query: I need to modernize an entire aging internal platform in one coordinated push — the interface, the internals, the data layer, and how it talks to other systems — rather than patching pieces separately over time.
rationale: caller wants the full multi-front modernization sprint bundled as one effort, not a single facet

query: want the multi-agent setup to remember what worked on past runs and adapt for this kind of task, not just spin up a blank network layout every time
rationale: wants workflow-pattern-level learning and persistence across runs, distinct from swarm-orchestration's topology/load-balancing focus

query: I'm restructuring our system into cleanly separated business areas, each owning its own core objects and firing events when something important happens inside it, instead of one tangled shared model.
rationale: caller wants bounded-context/aggregate-root/domain-event structuring applied to the platform's architecture

query: My agents currently have three different memory systems that don't talk to each other and I want them collapsed into one consistent layer.
rationale: caller wants disparate memory subsystems merged into a single coherent layer, distinct from building a new distributed store or the whole platform bundle

query: I want to be able to ask how the pieces of this codebase actually connect to each other, not just get back text snippets that mention similar words.
rationale: caller wants structural relationship mapping over the codebase rather than plain text/semantic search

query: Pull together API docs for every route in this backend, based on what's already annotated in the code.
rationale: caller wants endpoint documentation auto-derived from controller annotations, not a generic project README
